rows: What is Artemis 3 and why is it hard?

First crewed lunar landing since 1972; crew flies SLS/Orion to Gateway, transfers to SpaceX Starship HLS for surface landing at south pole; hard because Starship HLS requires multiple in-orbit refueling flights not yet demonstrated, and lunar south pole precision landing is new
Why does NASA focus on lunar south pole?

Water ice in permanently shadowed craters (confirmed by LCROSS/LRO); adjacent ridges have near-continuous solar power; water → O₂ for breathing + H₂ for propellant → enables cislunar economy; very different geology from Apollo equatorial sites
What is Mars Sample Return and why is it in trouble?

NASA+ESA plan to retrieve Perseverance's samples from Mars surface and return to Earth; original cost estimate grew to $8-11B; schedule slipped to 2030s+; independent review forced redesign; critical for life-detection science but faces budget pressure
What is Europa Clipper looking for?

Signs of habitability in Europa's confirmed subsurface ocean; 50 flybys characterizing ice shell, ocean chemistry, geological activity, and whether conditions could support life; no lander — orbital survey only
What are the three hardest unsolved problems for human Mars missions?

(1) Landing 100+ tonnes on Mars surface — too thin for parachutes, too massive for current retropropulsion; (2) Radiation — ~1000 mSv round trip exceeds NASA career limits; (3) VIIP — 70% of ISS astronauts get eye damage with no known countermeasure

Proposal to use a GW-class Earth-based laser to push gram-scale light sails to 20% c for a flyby of Proxima Centauri; 20-year travel time; 4+ year data return delay; currently proof-of-concept R&D, not near-term mission
Why is the Moon a stepping stone to Mars?

Proves ISRU technology (water → propellant); proves human long-duration operations outside LEO; tests Starship architecture; provides propellant depot for deep space; ~3-day abort distance vs 6+ months for Mars
